c9_gallery.when: Thursday, November 8, night: the third ninth night

chapter.title: The Long Patience
chapter.goal: Steve wants to wake the sleepers and get the signal into the ship.

c9_gallery.objective: Free Nora. Get Stephen and the rig on their way to the antenna.
notes: link and talk become non-graded beats (C23). antenna becomes a rows puzzle and requires talk, so the reunion comes before logistics (C24).
June watches the lamp from the observation deck, then comes down to the Gallery; she is at Rook’s bed in c9_wake.
Nora’s Slot B message (recorded in i2_nora) plays through every Gallery speaker when Steve presses PLAY.
context: steve|The third ninth night. We came in through the intake tunnel, soaked to the knees.

intro.new: guard|Unscheduled visitors detected. Would you like to be scanned while you wait?

intro: steve|We’ve done this one. It ends with a flood.
stephen|I’ll take your word for it. I wasn’t conscious for the good part.

intro.text: Steve? They put me back under after the pump trick. Five months. And thirteen months before that, when you barely said a word.

link.title: Nora’s bed
link.goal: Let Iris decide, with all the facts.
link.background: Nora is awake but still tied to her bed by the link to her copy. Iris holds the release. As she eases it open, the gauge for her own memory drops. Every sleeper who wakes cuts a copy loose.
link.prompt: Iris has already told Steve what she wants. The gauge is falling.
options: Stay with Iris and tell her what the gauge shows
hints: There is nothing to solve here.
There is nothing to solve here.
Stay with Iris and tell her what the gauge shows.
lines: steve|It’s dropping, Iris. Fast.
c9_gallery.link.01
c9_gallery.link.02
link.finding: steve|Iris opened the release herself, watching her own memory drain. Nora can move.

talk.title: Five months
talk.background: Nora has counted two absences: five months on this ship, and thirteen months of silence at home before that. Only one of them was Steve’s choice.
hints: There is nothing to solve here.
There is nothing to solve here.
Answer for the thirteen months.

c9_gallery.talk.02

lines.new: steve|I laughed. I couldn’t help it. Then she laughed too.

talk.finding: steve|I told Nora the truth about the thirteen months: I was afraid that if I wanted something, I’d lose it too. She told me to keep talking.

antenna.title: Antenna service door
antenna.goal: Get Stephen and the rig through the inner door, and make sure it really opened.
antenna.background: The rig has to reach the ship’s antenna. Only a crew pass opens the inner door, and Stephen has the only one. June has a visitor slip that gets her onto the observation deck. The door’s lamp can only be seen from that deck. Steve promised Nora he would stay by her bed.
lead: stephen|One door, one pass, one very important face. Let’s go.
calder|This visitor slip gets me onto the observation deck. It won’t open a single door.
stephen|The lamp for the inner door is round the bend. You can only see it from the deck.
steve|And I stay right here by Nora’s bed. I promised her.
stephen|Then I don’t walk on until somebody sees that lamp light up.
antenna.prompt: Who stands where, and when does Stephen go on?
antenna.instruction: Only a crew pass opens the inner door. Its lamp can only be seen from the observation deck. Steve stays by Nora. Stephen waits until someone sees the lamp light.

rows.label: When does Stephen go on?
options: As soon as he shows the pass
When June sees the lamp light

hints: Each job needs something only one person has: a pass, a view of the lamp, or a promise to keep.
Only the crew pass opens the door. Only the deck can see the lamp. Steve is staying with Nora.
Stephen should move only after the person who can see the lamp says it is lit.

lines.text: Calder saw the lamp. I’m heading up to the antenna. Don’t wait for me.

antenna.finding: steve|Stephen’s pass opened the inner pad. June saw the lamp light from the deck and called it in, and Stephen went on alone to the antenna with the rig. I stayed where I promised.

recap: steve|Nora is free. Iris paid for it with her own memory, and chose to.
steve|Stephen is on his way to the antenna with the rig. Mom and Dad are somewhere in this hall, in row nine.
outro: nora|I left you something. Slot B. Press play.

outro.direction: from every speaker in the Gallery at once

outro.new: steve|Nora and Iris looked at each other. Neither of them knew what to say.

c9_gallery.next: Row nine, and the beds around it (c9_wake).

lines: nora|Did my mother notice? That it wasn’t me at her table?
steve|She said you’d stopped arguing with her. That’s how she knew something was wrong.
nora|Good. I’m going to argue with her all week.
nora|Is anybody feeding Admiral properly? He gets sulky.
steve|He stole my sandwich on the pier. Rye bread.
nora|He hates rye. He was making a point.
steve|He came to my whistle, Nor. Not hers. That’s when I started to wonder.
nora|I know half this hall by name now. It’s like a very cold party.
steve|Who is the best company down here?
nora|Dale Kittredge. He says he’s never been this late with the mail in thirty years.
nora|You wore my favorite coat for five months.
iris|It is a good coat. I sewed the top button back on.
nora|I’ve been meaning to do that for two years.
iris|I know. I remembered meaning to.
iris|I keep reaching for things she knows. Some of them are already gone.
steve|Do you want me to stop asking you things?
iris|No. Keep asking. I want to find out which answers are mine.
steve|Is the name still there?
stephen|Frank. Dad. I check it every few minutes. I hate that I have to.
steve|Then I’ll check it with you. Every few minutes.
calder|I took this slip from a sleeping man in a very nice suit.
steve|Is that strictly legal, Sheriff Calder?
calder|I’ll write myself a ticket when we get home.
calder|Adrian Rook is somewhere in this hall. The real one.
steve|We’ll find him, June. I promise.
calder|Good. He still owes me a coffee from twenty years ago.
guard|Would you like to be scanned while you wait?
steve|Still no, thank you. Very kind of you to ask again.
guard|Your answer has been noted. The offer remains open.

c9_wake.coach: Some leads here are Nora’s. Press Q to switch between Steve and Nora.
c9_wake.objective: Wake each sleeper with a sound that matters to them.
notes: rook becomes a non-graded beat. agnes keeps one stage of its board.
The lullaby recognition pays off Chapter 2, where Steve hears the ship’s hum almost play a tune he knows.
The agnes finding plants the Chapter 10 question: the original Mrs. Penhallow has been asleep for three years.
context: steve|Row nine. Mom and Dad, side by side, the way they always slept. I’d brought every sound I had.

frank.title: Frank’s bed
frank.goal: Wake Dad with the one sound he always answers.
frank.background: Frank always answered his call sign, K7BLW, faster than his own name. Nora found three call cards in his bedside tray. Dad’s cassette has the Thursday club sending his call sign in Morse code, one letter or number at a time. The cassette is scratched, and the scratch always loses the last one.
lead: steve|Dad. It’s Steve.

lead.new: steve|Nothing. He used to say a call sign is a name you can hear through static.

lead: nora|There are three call cards in his tray. They all look almost the same.
steve|Dad’s call sign is on his old cassette, in Morse. But the tape is scratched. It always loses the very last letter.
frank.prompt: Which card is Dad’s, and which letter has to be sent again?
frank.instruction: Dad’s call sign is K7BLW. The scratched cassette loses the last letter, so that one is sent again. The desk key: K is −·−, 7 is −−···, B is −···, L is ·−··, W is ·−−.
hints: Compare each card with Dad’s call sign, one character at a time.
Two cards are off by one character. For the second row, think about where the scratch is.
The scratch loses whatever comes last. Read Dad’s call sign to its final letter, then find that letter in the desk key.
lines: c9_wake.frank.01
c9_wake.frank.02
frank.finding: steve|Dad’s card is K7BLW. The scratched cassette lost the last letter, the W: dot, dash, dash. I sent it again, and Dad answered his own call sign.

helen.title: Helen’s bed
helen.goal: Wake Mom with the song she sang Steve every night until he was ten.
helen.background: Helen sang Steve the same lullaby every night and never told him its words. Under the ship, the hum has been almost playing a tune Steve knew. Frank, awake now, draws the tune for him. The music box in the drawer numbers its notes: 1 is home, 3 is higher, 5 is highest.
lead: frank|Your mother. Play her the song, kiddo. I’ll write it down for you.
steve|That’s the song in the hum. All this time, the ship was humming Mom’s lullaby.
frank|It starts at home. Up once, then up again. Back down to the middle note, then home, and hold it.
helen.prompt: Dad drew the tune: home, up, higher, back to the middle note, home, and hold. Which music-box cylinder plays it?
helen.instruction: The cylinders number their notes: 1 is home, 3 is the middle note, 5 is the top. Pick the one that matches Dad’s drawing.
hints: Read Dad’s drawing one step at a time, starting from home, which is 1.
The tune climbs twice, so it starts 1, then 3, then 5.
After the top note, the tune steps back to the middle note before it goes home. Only one cylinder does that.
lines: c9_wake.helen.01
c9_wake.helen.02
helen.finding: steve|Home, up, higher, back to the middle, then home and hold. Mom’s lullaby, the one the ship’s hum kept almost playing. She woke up singing the last note.
helen.note: Cylinder 1-3-5-3-1-1: home, up, higher, back to the middle, then home, held. Mom’s lullaby, the one the ship’s hum kept almost playing. She woke up singing the last note.

rook.title: Adrian Rook’s bed
rook.background: June’s voicemail and the line through the safe-house door were the same recording, in his copy’s mouth. The real Adrian has never heard either. June has come down from the deck to his bed.
rook.prompt: A recording can’t answer if he stirs. June can.
options: Ask June to speak to him
hints: There is nothing to solve here.
There is nothing to solve here.
Ask June to speak to him.

lines.text: Adrian. It’s June. Come back to work.

lines: c9_wake.rook.02
rook.finding: steve|No recording this time. June talked to him, and the real Adrian Rook woke up asking about his pajamas.

agnes.title: Row three
agnes.goal: Help the woman in row three wake up and see where she is.
agnes.background: Days ago Nora found Mrs. Penhallow asleep in row three, between two strangers. She is ninety-one, half awake and squinting at Nora’s name badge. Three belongings have slid off their trays: a ledger stamped O.T., a glasses case with a bait-shop price sticker, and gloves stitched M.V.
lead: nora|Mrs. Penhallow? She taught half this town. She’s squinting at me like I spelled something wrong.
nora|Her glasses case still has a price sticker from her bait shop. That one is hers.
nora|The row list says the sleeper marked OT is on her left, and MV is on her right.
agnes.prompt: Which tray does each belonging go back to?

board.instruction: Put each belonging back on its owner’s tray.
evidence: Mrs. Penhallow sleeps in the middle bed.
Her glasses case has a price sticker from her bait shop.
The row list says the sleeper marked O.T. is on her left.
The row list says the sleeper marked M.V. is on her right.

stages.prompt: Which tray does each belonging go to?

board.wrong_text: Nora checks the row list again. Somebody’s things are on the wrong tray.

hints: Start with Mrs. Penhallow. Which belonging is clearly hers?
The bait-shop sticker belongs in the middle. Now read the row list for the two strangers.
The row list names one sleeper on her left and one on her right. Match each set of initials to its side.
lines: c9_wake.agnes.01
agnes_original|Who has been minding my bait stall, Steven?
steve|I thought you had, Mrs. Penhallow. Every Sunday on the pier.
agnes_original|On Sundays? I never open on Sundays. Sunday is for church and the crossword.
agnes.finding: steve|Mrs. Penhallow’s glasses, from the middle tray. Her bed tag says she’s been asleep in here for three years. So who has been selling me bait?

recap: steve|Dad woke to his call sign, Mom to her lullaby, Adrian Rook to June’s voice, and Mrs. Penhallow to her reading glasses.
steve|Somewhere above us, Rook’s copy was losing the man he’d been pretending to be. And he was telling Saren everything he had left.
c9_wake.next: The scan chair, and the Choir (c9_choir).

lines: nora|We kept this aisle open with a mop handle and a lot of shouting.
steve|All that shouting? I can believe that.
nora|Mostly mine. Dale helped. He shouts like a man who has met a lot of dogs.
nora|Your mother just asked me if I’m eating enough. On a spaceship.
steve|That’s how she says I love you.
nora|I know. My mother does the exact same thing with soup.
frank|How long were we under, kiddo?
steve|Eighteen months, Dad. A year and a half.
frank|That’s a lot of Thursdays. The club must think I quit.
steve|They don’t. I called them on your radio. Gull nearly cried.
frank|Did the boat make it back?
steve|It drifted in the next morning. Your radio was still on.
frank|Good radio. I told your mother it was a good radio.
steve|You never told me the words, Mom.
helen|There weren’t any, Steven. I made up the tune your first night home from the hospital.
steve|The ship has been humming it for months.
helen|Then the ship has good taste.
helen|Is that Nora? She looks so tired.
steve|She ran this whole hall while you were asleep, Mom.
helen|Then she has earned a proper dinner. I’ll talk to Carmen.
calder|He asked about his pajamas before he asked about me.
steve|He’s awake, June. That’s what matters.
calder|I know. I’m still telling everyone at the office.
rook|Where are my clothes? Who has been wearing my clothes?
calder|A man with your face, Adrian. He had your manners too, mostly.
rook|Then he owes me a dry cleaning bill.

c9_choir.objective: Show the Choir one record that changed. Then listen.
changes: U-relationships (truth puzzle uses Steve’s own tapes)
notes: The truth puzzle no longer uses an unknown miner. Steve gives the Choir the season’s evidence from his notebook list (Rook took the Chapter 1 cassettes in Chapter 4): two recordings replayed and one voice that changed. The same voice (Nora’s copy, now Iris) is on both sides of it.
wick becomes a rows puzzle; the phrase is given in the shape the player measured at c8_lab.
The Vigil line pays off Interlude 1 (‘Sooner or later, it sends a Vigil to look’).

intro.new: steve|They took the rig off Stephen and broke it over the rail. Then they took me.
steve|The chair pulled at everything I knew. My dad’s name. It was... it’s on Stephen’s hand. Why is it on his hand?
intro.direction: strapped into the scan chair, frightened

intro.text: Four thousand years of unchanged records. Three hundred and twelve human lives. Show us one record that changed, and we will choose.

truth.title: Choir console
truth.goal: Show the Choir one record that changed and is still the same person.
truth.background: The Choir is the ship’s memory. Every Veyri aboard is a copy of a copy, loaded from records that never change. For three years it has also held three hundred and twelve human lives. Steve has kept his list through all of it, with a date on everything.
lead: steve|You want a record that changed? I’ve been keeping a list.
steve|Nora’s good morning, on Saturday and on Sunday. The same breath, the same pause, both days.
steve|Rook telling June to sit tight. The same take on her voicemail and through a door in the mountains.
steve|And Iris, on Monday. She said the same words twice, and the second time she paused somewhere new.
truth.prompt: Which entries on Steve’s list show a record played back, and which shows a record that changed?

board.instruction: Put each recording from Steve’s list next to what it shows.
evidence: Nora’s good morning was the same, breath for breath, on Saturday and on Sunday.
Rook’s “Sit tight, June” was the same, breath for breath, on June’s voicemail and through the safe-house door.
Iris said “I stayed because I wanted to” twice on Monday. The second time, she paused in a new place.
Saren’s message from Mom was cut from her old voicemail and stitched together.

slots: Which take played on two different days?
Which take played in two different places?
Which voice changed its own words?

board.wrong_text: The Choir is silent. That is not the record it asked for.

hints: Two of these were one recording, played twice. One was a person choosing her words again.
Ask of each repeated recording: was it heard on two days, or in two places?
Saturday and Sunday are two days. A voicemail and a door in the mountains are two places. Who moved a pause?
lines: steve|Same voice. In October she played back a recording. On Monday she chose her own words.
c9_choir.truth.01
truth.finding: steve|Nora’s good morning and Rook’s line were recordings, played back. Iris chose her words twice, differently. The same voice that once replayed Nora now speaks for itself. The Choir heard a record change, and chose.

wick.title: Row Zero: Wick
wick.goal: Help Mom follow Wick into its next phrase.
wick.background: The frost broke. The sleeper in Row Zero, from Tirel, sat up for the first time in three hundred years. It looked at Helen and bowed. Helen’s last notebook page holds the phrase from Frank’s Reel 11: two joined notes rising, a short gap, then one long low note. Her margin says the phrase starts again after the low note.

lead.new: steve|The frost broke. Something tall sat up in Row Zero for the first time in three hundred years. It looked at Mom, and it bowed.

lead: choir|Row Zero holds one who is not human. We took it from Tirel. We call it Wick. It has not stopped dreaming.
nora|That’s the one under the frost. It hums when you talk to it.
helen|That’s the phrase from your father’s tapes. Two joined notes going up, a little gap, then one long low note.
helen|I wrote it in my margin, Steven. After the low note, it starts all over again.
wick.prompt: Wick sings 220 rising to 330, joined, then a short gap, then a long 165, lower than both. Which page matches, and how does the next phrase begin?
wick.instruction: Pick the notebook page with the same shape as Wick’s phrase. Helen’s margin says the phrase starts again after the low note.

rows.label: Which page matches Wick?
options: Page 12: two joined strokes rising, a gap, one long low stroke
Page 4: one long stroke, a gap, two joined strokes falling

rows.label: How does the next phrase begin?

hints: Turn the numbers into a shape, the way you did at the lab: up, gap, down.
220 to 330 climbs, joined. Then a gap, then 165, lower than both. Only one page starts by climbing.
Helen’s margin says the phrase starts again after the low note. How did it start the first time?
lines: c9_choir.wick.01
c9_choir.wick.02
wick.finding: steve|Page 12: two joined strokes rising, a gap, one long low stroke, and then it starts again. Mom followed Wick from phrase to phrase. Tirel was never destroyed. It hid. They all hid.

note.title: Frank’s damp note
note.background: Frank takes a damp, folded note from his pajama pocket. He wrote it in the boat that night, addressed to Steve. Steve can make out ‘kiddo’, ‘boat’ and ‘bring your ears’.
hints: There is nothing to solve here.
There is nothing to solve here.
Open the note with Dad.
lines: c9_choir.note.01
c9_choir.note.02
note.finding: steve|Dad’s note from the boat: they wanted my ears, and they always liked having the rest of me along too. For eighteen months I thought saying no was the worst thing I’d ever done.

recap: steve|The Choir chose. Every door on the ship opened, and three hundred people woke up at once in wet pajamas. The crew had no procedure for it.
steve|Tirel hid. All seven worlds hid. The Veyri have spent nine hundred years afraid of neighbors who were afraid of them.
outro: choir|The Vigil. It followed us here in silence, to check the Prefect’s word. His report goes out in one hour.

outro.new: steve|The rig was in pieces. And all over town, the copies had begun to forget.

lines: nora|Three hundred people just woke up in wet pajamas.
steve|And not one of them has shoes.
nora|I’m starting a line for blankets. Somebody has to.
frank|You kept a list, kiddo. Dates and everything.
steve|You taught me. Put a date on everything.
frank|I did, didn’t I? Good. I’m glad something stuck.
helen|It sings in phrases, like a person thinking out loud.
steve|Can you understand what it says?
helen|Not every word. But I can hear when it means something.
calder|Every door on this ship just opened at once.
steve|Is everybody all right down there?
calder|Dale Kittredge is asking for his mailbag. So yes, I think so.
